title: Modelling Crypto Asset Price Dynamics, Optimal Crypto Portfolio, and Crypto Option Valuation

extraction.methodology_summary: The authors study the top seven crypto assets using daily closing prices and model log returns with multivariate ARMA(1,1)-GARCH(1,1) processes combined with various joint innovation distributions (multivariate t, multivariate variance-gamma, and t-copulas). Using Monte Carlo backtesting, they find the ARMA-GARCH model with Gaussian innovations and a multivariate t distribution (5 degrees of freedom) performs best. They construct minimum-risk portfolios via mean-variance (min Variance) and CVaR (min CVaR) optimizations and value European options on these crypto portfolios using an Esscher transform to pass to the equivalent martingale measure under NIG innovations.
extraction.universe: The top seven crypto assets (bitcoin, ethereum, XRP, litecoin, bitcoin cash, EOS, binance coin) selected by market capitalization, with SPY as the benchmark.

key_findings: Crypto portfolios constructed via optimizations that minimize variance and Conditional Value at Risk can outperform a major stock market index (the S&P 500).
Bitcoin acts as a risk diversifier while EOS acts as a risk contributor in the crypto portfolios.
The min CVaR portfolio has the highest risk-adjusted return among the tested portfolios, whereas the min Variance portfolio performs similarly to the S&P 500 benchmark.
A fair valuation model for European options on crypto asset indexes can be successfully formulated using an ARMA-GARCH model with normal inverse Gaussian innovations via the Esscher transform.
limitations: Assumes no transaction costs so that portfolio weights can be adjusted purely for hedging risk.
